subject: Request: temporary overnight SLA exception & contingency checklist
messages:
From: Michael Park <michael@starlite.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Increasing overnight latency incidents — ask for temporary SLA exception

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking my note last week. We saw two P1s overnight (03:20 and 04:05 PST) on Oct 19–20 where model serving latency spiked above our agreed P1 guardrails and caused a partial degradation of our ingestion pipeline. Our engineering team traced the root cause to queue buildup during scheduled index jobs in our SFO region, which overlaps Redwood's shared-hosted pool.

Given the recurrence and the upcoming holiday maintenance window (Oct 25–27), we need to request a short-term change to the overnight response terms while we stabilize: specifically, a temporary carveout for the local overnight window (00:00–06:00 PST) that relaxes the P2 and P1 hard-response SLA penalties and allows a tiered on-call cadence (one on-call engineer in region + a global fallback) for up to two weeks.

We want this to be limited in scope and timeboxed, and we expect to provide incident logs and the remediation plan from our side. Can you confirm if Redwood can authorize this and what the process looks like (forms, approvals, credits)?

Attached: incident-log-starlite-20271020.txt (minor redaction).

Thanks,
Michael
VP, Platform Engineering
Starlite AI

---
Attachment: incident-log-starlite-20271020.txt (text, 32KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Michael Park <michael@starlite.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Increasing overnight latency incidents — ask for temporary SLA exception

Hi Michael — thanks for the detail and for the log. I’m looping in Ben (sales/CS lead) and Irene (Head of Support Ops) so we can move quickly.

Short answers up front: yes, we can support a timeboxed temporary carveout with an agreed contingency checklist and a lower-penalty SLA profile for the 00:00–06:00 PST window for up to 14 days while you complete the mitigation. We’ll need:

- A completed SLO exception form (we can fill on our side, I’ve attached a draft).
- Confirmation of the exact start/end dates (you proposed Oct 25–Nov 7?).
- A mutual action plan (MAP) listing customer and Redwood remediation owners and runbook handoffs.
- Access to the incident telemetry you referenced (we received the log).

Operational notes / proposed contingency (high level):
- For the exception window we propose: 1) designate a single Redwood regional on-call (Pacific hours) plus a global P1 fallback; 2) enable a temporary elevated routing to dedicated instances for your account during the 00:00–06:00 PST window (subject to capacity); 3) waive penalty credits for verified infra-related queuing events while mutual MAP is in effect.

Ben, can you confirm contract language (credits/penalty waiver) and whether we should propose a small one-off credit for the recent incidents?

Irene, can you review the attached draft SLO exception form and the suggested roster in support_roster_q4.xlsx? If you can sign off today, I’ll send the formal exception and MAP to Michael and run the DocuSign for an exec sig.

Michael — once we have Irene's signoff I’ll send the formal doc and a short checklist you can use to validate readiness before we start the carveout.

—Vanessa
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — quick note on commercial terms.

We can accept the waiver for penalty credits for up to two weeks provided Starlite: 1) executes the exception form; 2) agrees to the MAP that includes proactive scaling thresholds; and 3) accepts a nominal one-time service credit equivalent to one week of average usage as a good-faith gesture (this offsets churn risk). The team prefers a credit rather than changing baseline SLOs permanently.

If Michael agrees to the start date of Oct 25 and end date of Nov 7, I’ll prepare the amendment language (short addendum to the Master Services Agreement) and route it through legal. We should note this as "timeboxed carveout — monitoring & rollback conditions".

Irene — operationally we’ll need coverage details by EOD so we can roster the regional on-call and the fallback. Vanessa, happy to support the DocuSign flow.

—Ben
Director of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Michael Park <michael@starlite.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Increasing overnight latency incidents — ask for temporary SLA exception

Adding operational approval. Vanessa, Ben — I reviewed the draft SLO exception form and the proposed roster. Approve contingent on the following checklist being signed by Starlite ops before the carveout starts:

1) MAP completed with named owners and on-call phone numbers for customer and Redwood.
2) Confirmed capacity burst plan (Starlite to allow temporary elevated routing to dedicated instances during 00:00–06:00 PST).
3) Daily 09:00 PST sync for the duration of the carveout (first 3 business days mandatory).
4) Starlite to provide retained telemetry and access to recent ingestion queue metrics (we received one log; we need continuous capture).
5) Incident escalation flow added to the playbook (Redwood regional on-call -> Redwood global fallback -> Starlite on-call escalation).

I’ll sign the SLO exception once the MAP is attached and the DocuSign has the start/end dates. Michael — if you can confirm Oct 25–Nov 7 and return the filled MAP by EOD Monday (Oct 24), we’ll execute and have the carveout ready for the 25th start.

I’m also attaching the completed SLO exception form (signed page) for speed.

Irene Choi
Head of Support Operations, Redwood Inference
